Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

admire verb

also admiration, look up to, admirable, admirer

classical

Cic. de Or. 1.20 fin.: ingenium tuum, Crasse, vehementer admīrāns (Lewis & Short)
Hor. Ep. 1.6.1
Traupman 149

admīror, admīrārī, admīrātus sum

verb, first conjugation, deponent, with accusative

admire; wonder at

To regard with admiration, of a person, a talent, a deed; just as often to be surprised at something (admīrātus sum brevitātem epistulae, Cic. Att. 6.9), so the context decides. Admīrātiō is admiration, admīrābilis admirable (see wonderful).

Other words

  • suspiciō, suspicere, suspexī, suspectum — look up to, esteem

    verb, third conjugation (-iō), transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 2.36: eōs virōs suspiciunt maximīsque efferunt laudibus (Lewis & Short); Traupman 341

    Literally to look up at; of people, to look up to, the opposite of dēspicere. Its other common sense is to suspect, so make the context plain.

  • mīror, mīrārī, mīrātus sum — wonder at, marvel at; admire

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical

    The plain verb for being surprised or amazed; it means admire only where the context makes the wonder approving.

  • admīrātiō, admīrātiōnis f. — admiration

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 149

  • admīrābilis, admīrābile — admirable

    declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.2: admīrābilis in dīcendō vir (Lewis & Short); Traupman 269

Examples

  • nīl admīrārī prope rēs est ūna, Numīcī, sōlaque quae possit facere et servāre beātum

    to be dazzled by nothing, Numicius, is almost the one and only thing that can make a man happy and keep him soHor. Ep. 1.6.1–2 (Lewis & Short)

  • paulisper alter alterīus cōnspectū, admīrātiōne mūtuā prope attonitī, conticuēre

    for a little while they were silent, almost stunned with admiration at the sight of each otherLiv. 30.30.2

  • eōs virōs suspiciunt maximīsque efferunt laudibus

    such men they look up to and praise to the skiesCic. Off. 2.36 (Lewis & Short)

See also wonderful.
